frozen_original.synopsis: After federal courts blocked the original Muslim ban, Trump signed a revised version on March 6, 2017, Executive Order 13780, which removed Iraq from the list and added exemptions for green card holders and existing visa holders. Courts again blocked the order, with federal judges in Hawaii and Maryland issuing nationwide injunctions before it could take effect. The Fourth and Ninth Circuit Courts of Appeals upheld the injunctions, ruling the order likely violated the Establishment Clause of the First Amendment. The administration framed the continued legal battles as judicial overreach. Critics saw the second version as merely cosmetic changes to an unconstitutional religious targeting policy.
frozen_original.title: Muslim Ban 2.0 — Executive Order 13780

proposal.description_long: On March 6, 2017, President Donald Trump signed Executive Order 13780, “Protecting the Nation from Foreign Terrorist Entry into the United States,” replacing his January order. The revised order suspended entry for 90 days by nationals of Iran, Libya, Somalia, Sudan, Syria and Yemen, subject to stated exceptions, and set a separate 120-day pause on refugee admissions. Iraq was no longer among the six countries. The order stated an effective time of March 16, 2017. Before that date, a federal district court in Hawaii temporarily blocked key provisions; a Maryland district court also enjoined parts of the order, and the government appealed. The Ninth Circuit’s opinion concerns the scope of the Hawaii injunction and should not be collapsed into the separate Maryland case. The order text and opinions are the relevant evidence for its provisions and litigation chronology. The AP URL attached to the original entry is a fact-check about Trump’s tweets and votes, not this order, so it cannot substantiate the existing description. This account describes the order and court challenges without treating the different injunctions as one ruling or suggesting the entire order was permanently invalidated at that stage.
proposal.description_medium: President Donald Trump signed Executive Order 13780 on March 6, 2017, revising his earlier travel restrictions. It imposed a 90-day entry suspension for nationals of Iran, Libya, Somalia, Sudan, Syria and Yemen, subject to exceptions, and separately paused refugee admissions. Iraq was removed from the covered-country list. Federal courts enjoined key provisions before or as the order was scheduled to take effect; those rulings came through separate cases and were later reviewed on appeal.
